keep: Lead with a specific, high-intent Indian document pain point (Aadhaar/e-PAN password, PDF too big, edit PDF). The top 3 reels are all concrete 'how do I do X' utility topics, and unlock_aadhaar is first at 1966 views and 24 saves.

Use a direct question or 'what if' hook in Hinglish that names the exact document, e.g. 'Aadhaar PDF ka password kya hota hai?'. The top reel is the only one that combines a question hook, a named document and an emoji.
Pick topics people save or share. The top reel got 24 saves and 18 shares. pdf_to_word got 12 saves. Save and share counts track the high scores better than likes do.
Keep the hook so that watchers stay past about 8s. The top 4 reels average 8.2–9.2s of watch time, against 3.4–3.5s for the bottom 2. Fast payoff on the answer seems to matter.
Use a broad 'one website for all your PDF/photo work' framing with the 👇 CTA. passport_photo, with a manual format, still ranked 4th at 919 views.
avoid: Generic task hooks with no pain point or named document, e.g. 'PDF ka table Excel mein kaise layein?' and 'Photos ko ek PDF kaise banayein?'. These are the bottom two at about 120 views and 3.4s average watch time, and they got almost no saves or shares.

Off-topic or curiosity hooks unrelated to the tool, such as 'Charging 100% tak mat karo' (resize_image_kb) and the Egypt honey story (unlock_pdf). The hook doesn't match the payload, so both sit at 220–435 views.
English-only abstract claims such as 'Most people think a PDF page can't become a photo'. It got 187 views and no saves or shares, which is weak next to the Hinglish pain-point hooks.
Niche, low-demand conversions (pdf_to_excel, image_to_pdf, pdf_to_jpg) as stand-alone reels. All three are under 190 views.
Reading too much into the posting delay. Only 4 of 11 reels are marked 0s or 20s, and the data doesn't separate timing from topic.
next_tests: Repeat the winning pattern on a sibling topic, with the same question hook and a named document: 'PAN card PDF ka password kya hota hai?' or 'Form 16 / bank statement PDF password'. Compare it with unlock_aadhaar to see if the topic or the format drives the views. unlock_pdf with an e-PAN hook got only 274 views, so this tests whether Aadhaar specifically is the draw.

Run the same topic (compress_pdf_kb) with two hooks: the 'What if...' English hook and a Hinglish question such as 'PDF 100KB se chhota kaise karein? Form reject ho raha hai?'. This isolates the effect of hook language and framing on a topic that already works.

Test the save and share CTA on a mid-performer, e.g. a 'Save this for your next form' line on pdf_to_word. Check whether saves and shares rise without hurting watch time. With 11 posts and one outlier, none of these results is proven yet.

keep: Lead with a concrete, relatable outcome in the hook. The best non-manual reel, 'Can one selfie become an ID photo?', got 446 views and 396 reach, and 9.4s average watch was the highest among all reels. This is a before/after on a single task, so it is the only structured format with any evidence behind it.

Use a single-task before/after demo on one tool. remove_background (same_task_before_after) was the top structured reel, with 446 views and 6.2s average watch. It is one reel, so this is a lead to test, not a proven rule.

Put a direct call to action to the website in the reel. The 'Please check our website too' reel had the highest watch time (9.4s) and 351 views. The result is mixed, because the same site-promo style ('Any PDF or photo job') had only 1.7s watch.

Make the reel shareable. The top-scoring reel, '#ilovedocuments', had 18 shares from 198 reach, far more than any other reel. It is a manual post, so it is unclear whether the cause is the content or the account's existing audience.

Use a story or question hook that holds attention. 'Why did Rohan miss his own interview?' held viewers for 8.2s, close to the best watch times, but it had few likes or saves. It is a retention signal only.
avoid: Generic, tool-list or 'any job' hooks. 'Any PDF or photo job – one free website' got only 1.7s average watch, the worst of all reels, and 133 views.
Cheat-sheet or bold-claim formats. 'Stop paying the cyber cafe for these 5 things' got 4.0s watch and 146 views. It did get 2 saves, the most of any reel, so it may suit saves more than reach.
Secret-answer how-to question hooks with no emotional stake. 'How do you send 4 photos as one PDF?' got 0 likes, 0 comments, 0 shares and 0 saves, and 7.0s watch did not turn into engagement.

Longer reels of about 30s or more without a payoff. All three of the weakest generated reels (30–32s) had 139–146 views, against 446 for the 21s reel. Length is mixed up with format here, so this is weak evidence.
Expecting comments. Only 1 comment appeared across all 7 reels, so no current hook is prompting conversation.
next_tests: Repeat the same_task_before_after format on a different tool, such as jpg_to_pdf or word_to_pdf, with a concrete outcome hook like 'selfie to ID photo'. Keep it near 20s to check whether the result is the format or just the remove_background topic.
Run the Rohan-style story hook on the same topic at about 20s with an explicit save or share prompt at the end. This tests whether the story's retention (8.2s) can be turned into saves or shares.

Make a cheat-sheet reel with a save-focused call to action ('save this for later'), plus a tighter hook than 'Stop paying the cyber cafe'. The format got 2 saves despite weak reach, so this tests whether it works as a saves format.
